key_insight: Droplet charge and vertical electric fields can accelerate collision-driven cloud droplet growth, potentially hastening warm rain initiation.
engineering_relevance: Charge- and field-dependent collision kernels could improve cloud microphysics models that predict droplet growth and rainfall onset.
method: Compute pair trajectories with droplet inertia, exact hydrodynamic interactions, electrostatic forces, and van der Waals forces.
Derive collision efficiencies for conducting droplets across charge states and vertical electric fields.
Evolve droplet distributions using a stochastic collection equation on a mass–charge grid.
evidence_signal: Simulations show an order-of-magnitude increase in uncharged-pair collision efficiency as the field rises from 5×10⁴ to 3×10⁵ V/m for larger-droplet radii of 10 or 20 μm; by 40 minutes, every electrified case has a larger-radius large-droplet mode than the hydrodynamic reference.
watch_item: The model considers spherical conducting droplets settling in still air, so applicability to turbulent clouds requires further validation.
paper_title: Electrostatic effects on settling cloud droplets: from pair collisions to size distribution evolution
